target: PDT-II (1)/(2)/(5): can a universal resource-normalized three-history defect inequality force associativity, n=3, or an experimentally distinctive bound?

theorem.statement: In every normed algebra with submultiplicative norm, ||[x,y,z]|| <= 2||x||||y||||z||.
theorem.proof: Triangle inequality gives ||(xy)z-x(yz)|| <= ||(xy)z||+||x(yz)||; submultiplicativity bounds each term by ||x||||y||||z||.

sharpness.statement: The universal constant 2 is sharp even for the real octonions with multiplicative norm.

candidate_no_go.candidate: A dimension-independent defect/resource bound obtained only from norm submultiplicativity and triangle inequality can exclude the octonionic n=7 sector or select n=3.
candidate_no_go.counterexample: The octonions satisfy ||xy||=||x||||y|| and saturate normalized defect 2 while remaining alternative and nonassociative.

prior_art_boundary: Submultiplicative normed algebras and the multiplicative octonion norm are established mathematics. The factor-2 associator bound is an immediate standard inequality; no mathematical novelty is claimed.
pdt_consequence: Any PDT experimentally distinctive composition inequality must contain additional PDT-native structure beyond norm submultiplicativity and triangle inequality.
next_obligation: Derive or falsify an independently motivated PDT coupling between normalized three-history defect and a measured revelation/resource quantity, then compare any induced probability law with QM/GPT under identical microscopic inputs.
